stories.title: Hreflang alternate links on all locale pages via generateMetadata
stories.description: All locale-prefixed pages (/en, /ms, /zh) must emit <link rel="alternate" hreflang="..."> tags pointing to sibling variants plus a canonical tag. Without these, Google treats the three URLs as duplicate content and may surface the wrong language to Malaysian users searching in Bahasa or Chinese.
acceptanceCriteria: Every public page renders <link rel="alternate" hreflang="en|ms|zh"> for all three locale variants in <head>
<link rel="canonical"> points to the current locale URL (not the default locale)
Google Rich Results Test confirms no hreflang errors on /en/menu and /en/ (home)
metadataBase is set in app/layout.tsx so Next.js resolves relative alternates to absolute URLs
generateMetadata helper is shared (DRY) across page.tsx files to avoid per-file duplication
technicalNotes: Use the `alternates` key in `generateMetadata` — Next.js App Router serialises this as <link rel="alternate" hreflang> in <head>
metadataBase must be set to NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL in root layout.tsx for absolute URL resolution
Create a shared `buildAlternates(path: string)` helper in src/lib/seo.ts that returns the alternates object for a given path segment
Verify with: curl -s https://site.com/en/menu | grep hreflang

stories.title: Multilingual sitemap alternateRefs via next-sitemap config
stories.description: The existing next-sitemap integration generates a basic sitemap.xml but does not include xhtml:link alternateRefs for multilingual pages. Google's sitemap spec supports per-URL language annotations (equivalent to hreflang in HTML) as a complementary signal alongside the <link> tags.
acceptanceCriteria: sitemap.xml includes <xhtml:link rel="alternate" hreflang="en|ms|zh" href="..."> for every locale variant of each URL
No duplicate locale prefixes in generated URLs (not /ms/ms/menu) — verified by viewing raw sitemap.xml
Sitemap is submitted to Google Search Console and shows no errors
next-sitemap postbuild script generates the sitemap without build failures
technicalNotes: Add `alternateRefs` array to the `transform` function in next-sitemap.config.js
Known issue: next-sitemap's built-in `i18n` config can produce duplicate prefixes — use a custom transform that manually builds alternateRefs from the locales array
Add xmlns:xhtml namespace declaration to <urlset> in sitemapSize or custom config
next-sitemap docs: https://github.com/iamvishnusankar/next-sitemap#alternaterefs
dependencies: Hreflang alternate links on all locale pages via generateMetadata

stories.title: On-demand menu cache invalidation via revalidateTag after admin edits
stories.description: The menu page uses time-based ISR (`revalidate = 3600`). When the admin changes a price, toggles availability, or updates an image via the admin panel, the customer-facing menu page stays stale for up to one hour. On-demand revalidation using `revalidateTag('menu')` would make changes visible within seconds of the admin saving.
acceptanceCriteria: After admin PATCHes a menu item (price, availability, image), the customer-facing /[locale]/menu reflects the change within 5 seconds on the next page load
PATCH /api/admin/menu/[id] calls revalidateTag('menu') server-side before returning the response
Menu data fetching in src/lib/menu.ts is wrapped with unstable_cache tagged 'menu'
Time-based revalidate = 3600 remains as a fallback safety net
Build does not fail on Vercel (unstable_cache requires Node.js runtime, not Edge)
technicalNotes: Use `import { unstable_cache } from 'next/cache'` to wrap the Neon DB query in src/lib/menu.ts
Tag the cache entry with `['menu']` and set `revalidate: 3600` as fallback
In PATCH /api/admin/menu/[id] route handler: `import { revalidateTag } from 'next/cache'; revalidateTag('menu');`
Also call revalidateTag('menu') from the sold-out toggle and display-category admin routes
Requires Node.js runtime (default on Vercel) — do not set `export const runtime = 'edge'` on these routes

stories.title: Order submission form validation via Server Action and Zod schema
stories.description: The pre-order modal currently validates the contact number and arrival time client-side only. These checks can be bypassed by direct API calls. Moving to a Server Action backed by a shared Zod schema provides server-side enforcement, consistent error messages, and the ability to re-use the schema for API route validation.
acceptanceCriteria: A Zod schema in src/lib/schemas/order.ts validates contactNumber (Malaysian regex 01X-XXXXXXX or 01XX-XXXXXXX), estimatedArrival (datetime, minimum 15 min from server time), and notes (max 200 chars optional)
Direct POST to /api/orders with an invalid phone number returns a 422 with field-level error details
Server-side validation rejects an estimatedArrival < 15 minutes from now even if client-side check was bypassed
The pre-order modal renders per-field error messages returned from the server
useActionState (React 19) is used in the modal component to bind the Server Action
technicalNotes: Malaysian mobile regex: /^01[0-9]-\d{7,8}$/ covers 010-1234567 (7 digits) and 016-12345678 (8 digits)
Server Action in src/app/actions/submit-order.ts — use 'use server' directive
useActionState replaces the deprecated useFormState in React 19 (project already on React 19)
Minimum arrival time: compare against new Date() + 15 * 60 * 1000 on server to prevent time-skew exploits
Return `{ errors: result.error.flatten().fieldErrors }` shape for client consumption

stories.title: INP optimisation: wrap menu filter in startTransition and lazy-load chat widget
stories.description: INP (Interaction to Next Paint) replaced FID as a Core Web Vital in March 2024 and is now a Google Search ranking factor. The menu filter pill click triggers a re-render of 50+ menu cards synchronously on the main thread, and the chat widget loads eagerly on every page. Both degrade INP beyond the 200ms good threshold on mid-range Android devices.
acceptanceCriteria: Menu filter pill click INP measured below 200ms on a Moto G Power (Lighthouse mobile simulation) before and after the change
Filter state update is wrapped in React.startTransition() so it does not block user input
ChatWidget is loaded via next/dynamic with { ssr: false } and only initialises after the page becomes interactive
Chrome DevTools Interactions lane shows no Long Animation Frame (LoAF) > 50ms on filter click
MenuCard components are memoised with React.memo to prevent full-grid re-renders on unrelated state changes
technicalNotes: import { startTransition } from 'react'; wrap setActiveFilter(category) call inside startTransition(() => { ... })
dynamic(() => import('@/components/chat/chat-widget'), { ssr: false }) in the locale layout
Add React.memo wrapper to MenuCard: export default React.memo(MenuCard)
Profile with Chrome DevTools > Performance > INP lane; look for 'Interaction' entries > 200ms
Reference: https://web.dev/articles/inp

stories.title: WCAG 2.2 redundant entry: pre-fill returning customer phone number from localStorage
stories.description: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 3.3.7 (Redundant Entry, Level A — legally required baseline) states that information entered in a prior step of the same process must not be re-entered unless essential. A returning customer who previously submitted a pre-order should not need to re-type their phone number.
acceptanceCriteria: On successful order submission, the customer's contact number is saved to localStorage key 'mm_contact_number'
When the pre-order modal opens on a subsequent visit, the contact number field is pre-filled with the stored value
The pre-filled value is editable — user can clear and retype without restriction
No phone number is stored in server-side session or cookie (localStorage only)
WCAG 2.2 criterion 3.3.7 is satisfied per manual audit checklist
technicalNotes: Criterion source: https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#redundant-entry
localStorage.setItem('mm_contact_number', contactNumber) in the order submission success handler
Read with useEffect on modal open: const saved = localStorage.getItem('mm_contact_number'); if (saved) setContactNumber(saved)
Pair with existing mm_order_history localStorage key for a consistent storage pattern

stories.title: WCAG 2.4.11 fix: focused form inputs not obscured by sticky tray and header bars
stories.description: WCAG 2.2 Success Criterion 2.4.11 (Focus Not Obscured Minimum, Level AA) requires that keyboard-focused UI elements are not entirely hidden by author-created sticky content such as a header or sticky footer. The floating tray bar and fixed header can fully obscure focused inputs in forms (pre-order modal, contact page) on short-viewport mobile screens.
acceptanceCriteria: Tab through the pre-order modal on a 568px-tall viewport — all focused inputs are at least partially visible and not entirely covered by sticky bars
The contact page form fields are not obscured by the header when tabbed to on mobile
CSS scroll-padding-top on the document root is set to at least the header height so scroll-into-view accounts for the fixed header
CSS scroll-padding-bottom is set to at least the tray bar height on pages that render the tray
Audit passes in axe DevTools or equivalent automated accessibility checker
technicalNotes: WCAG 2.2 criterion 2.4.11: https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/#focus-not-obscured-minimum
Add `scroll-padding-top: var(--header-height)` and `scroll-padding-bottom: var(--tray-height)` to <html> in globals.css
Define CSS custom properties --header-height (64px) and --tray-height (80px) in :root
Test with keyboard Tab key on mobile Chrome with DevTools device emulation at 568px height

stories.title: Menu item detail page and modal via Next.js Parallel and Intercepting Routes
stories.description: There is currently no per-item detail page or modal. Adding shareable item URLs (/en/menu/item/[id]) using Next.js Parallel Routes + Intercepting Routes gives each dish a dedicated page (for SEO and social sharing) while keeping the in-app experience modal-based (scroll position preserved, no full navigation). This enables food photography showcase and per-item structured data.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking a menu card from the /menu grid opens an overlay modal with the item photo, full description, price, allergen badges, and an Add to Tray button
The browser URL changes to /[locale]/menu/item/[id] when the modal opens, and returns to /[locale]/menu on close
Refreshing or sharing the URL /[locale]/menu/item/[id] renders a full standalone page (not modal) with the same content
The modal can be dismissed by pressing Escape, clicking the backdrop, or using the router.back() close button
The menu grid scroll position is preserved when the modal closes (user sees the same position they were at)
technicalNotes: File structure: app/[locale]/menu/@modal/(.)item/[id]/page.tsx (interceptor) + app/[locale]/menu/item/[id]/page.tsx (full page)
app/[locale]/menu/layout.tsx must accept and render both {children} and {modal} slots
Use router.back() for close — this dismisses the intercepted route without adding a new history entry
Share data-fetching logic via a MenuItemDetail component imported by both the modal and full-page variants
Requires Next.js 15+ for stable intercepting routes with dynamic segments — verify with current Next.js 16 version

stories.title: Touch 'n Go payment page: copy-to-clipboard button for TnG phone number
stories.description: The payment page displays the cafe's Touch 'n Go QR code and registered phone number. TnG eWallet's 'Pay Phone Number' feature allows customers to pay by entering the recipient's phone number directly without scanning a QR code — useful when the QR image fails to load or is hard to scan on a low-brightness screen. A one-tap copy button eliminates manual number transcription errors.
acceptanceCriteria: A 'Copy' icon button appears adjacent to the TnG phone number on the payment page
Clicking it writes the phone number to the clipboard using the Clipboard API
The button shows a 'Copied!' confirmation state for 2 seconds then resets
If the Clipboard API is unavailable (non-secure context), the button is hidden and the number remains selectable text
The phone number displayed and copied matches the tngPhone value from /api/settings
technicalNotes: Use navigator.clipboard.writeText(tngPhone).catch(() => {}) — Clipboard API requires HTTPS (Vercel satisfies this)
Feature-detect: `if (!navigator.clipboard) { hideCopyButton(); return; }`
Button state: use useState<'idle'|'copied'>; set 'copied' on success, setTimeout 2000ms back to 'idle'
tngPhone is already exposed via GET /api/settings — no new endpoint needed

stories.title: Placeholder image for menu items missing photos
stories.description: Menu items without a corresponding photo in public/images/menu/ currently display a broken image or empty space, creating a visually inconsistent and low-quality experience. A standardised branded placeholder maintains layout integrity and communicates 'photo coming soon' without breaking the grid.
acceptanceCriteria: Any menu item whose image file does not exist at /images/menu/{code}.jpg renders a branded placeholder (logo or food illustration on a warm cream background)
The placeholder is a static asset in public/images/ — no client-side error handling or broken img tags in the DOM
MenuCard and EditableMenuCard both use the same fallback logic
The placeholder respects the same aspect ratio (4:3 or configured ratio) as real food photos
Admin can replace the placeholder by uploading an image in the admin menu editor
technicalNotes: Next.js <Image> supports onError prop: `onError={() => setSrc('/images/menu-placeholder.jpg')}`
Alternatively, use a blurDataURL placeholder until the real image loads (pairs with LQIP story already in backlog)
Create public/images/menu-placeholder.jpg — a 400×300px branded image with the cafe's earthy warm palette
Add a MenuItemImage component that wraps next/image with the fallback logic, used by both MenuCard and EditableMenuCard

stories.title: Resource hints: preconnect to Neon Postgres host and Groq API
stories.description: Preconnect hints in <head> instruct the browser to resolve DNS, perform TLS handshake, and open a TCP connection to critical third-party origins before they are actually requested. The Neon database and Groq AI API are cold-connected on each function invocation, but for browser-originated requests (AI chat streaming), preconnect reduces Time to First Byte.
acceptanceCriteria: <link rel="preconnect" href="https://api.groq.com"> is present in the root layout <head> (required for the streaming chat API)
<link rel="dns-prefetch" href="https://api.groq.com"> is present as a fallback for browsers that do not support preconnect
Lighthouse report shows no 'Avoid multiple page redirects' or 'Preconnect to required origins' warnings for Groq
No preconnect hints are added for server-side-only origins (Neon) that the browser never directly contacts
technicalNotes: Only add preconnect for origins the browser contacts directly — Neon is server-side only (no preconnect needed)
Add in root app/layout.tsx inside <head> using Next.js metadata.other or directly in the JSX head section
Groq endpoint: https://api.groq.com — preconnect benefits the first chat message Time To First Token
If OpenRouter fallback is used: also add preconnect for https://openrouter.ai

stories.title: Admin JWT session expiry warning with one-click session refresh
stories.description: Admin JWT cookies expire silently. The admin may be mid-workflow (editing an order, uploading a menu image) when the session expires, and the next API call returns 401 — causing data loss if the form state is not preserved. A session expiry warning banner with a one-click refresh prevents silent logouts during active use.
acceptanceCriteria: A warning banner appears in the admin panel when fewer than 5 minutes remain on the JWT expiry
The banner includes a 'Renew Session' button that calls a /api/admin/refresh-session endpoint to issue a new JWT cookie
On successful refresh, the banner dismisses and the admin continues working without page reload
If the session expires without renewal, the admin is redirected to /admin/login with a 'Session expired' toast message
The JWT expiry time is readable from the cookie's exp claim client-side (no server round-trip needed to check)
technicalNotes: Decode the JWT's exp field client-side using atob(token.split('.')[1]) — no secret needed to read public claims
Use setInterval every 60s in a useAdminSession() hook to check remaining time
POST /api/admin/refresh-session — verify current token, issue new one with refreshed expiry, set-cookie in response
Requires reading the JWT cookie value client-side — consider setting it as httpOnly: false for this purpose, or expose the expiry separately via /api/admin/session-status
Store 'session expiring soon' UI state in a global admin context so it shows on all admin tabs

stories.title: Operating hours display on Contact and About pages from DB config
stories.description: The Contact and About pages currently hardcode cafe hours or omit them entirely. Operating hours are stored in data/operating-hours.json (and managed from the admin panel). Rendering live hours from the config on public-facing pages ensures accuracy when hours change (e.g. holiday adjustments) without requiring a code deployment.
acceptanceCriteria: The Contact page displays the current operating hours for each day of the week, sourced from data/operating-hours.json via getSiteSettings()
If today's hours are different from the default (holiday override), they are visually highlighted
The hours are rendered server-side (RSC) so they are crawlable by Google without JavaScript
The hours table/list is correctly translated in all three locales (day names and time format)
When admin updates operating hours in the admin panel, the change is visible on the Contact page within the ISR revalidation window
technicalNotes: getSiteSettings() already reads data/operating-hours.json — import it in the Contact page server component
Use Intl.DateTimeFormat with timeZone: 'Asia/Kuala_Lumpur' for time formatting consistency
Day names should use the i18n messages system (add keys like 'days.monday', 'days.tuesday' to messages/*.json)
Pair with schema.org openingHoursSpecification structured data already handled by the Restaurant JSON-LD story

stories.title: robots.txt configuration for Vercel deployment with admin panel exclusion
stories.description: A correctly configured robots.txt prevents search engine crawlers from indexing the admin panel, API routes, and internal paths while allowing indexing of all public-facing pages. Without it, Google may crawl /admin and /api/*, creating unnecessary crawl budget waste and potential information leakage in search index.
acceptanceCriteria: robots.txt disallows crawling of /admin, /api/, /en/admin, /ms/admin, /zh/admin
robots.txt allows all public pages: /, /[locale]/, /[locale]/menu, /[locale]/blog, /[locale]/about, /[locale]/contact
Sitemap URL is declared in robots.txt: Sitemap: https://[NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL]/sitemap.xml
robots.txt is served at the root URL with Content-Type: text/plain
Google Search Console shows no crawl errors introduced by the robots.txt rules
technicalNotes: In Next.js App Router, create app/robots.ts (TypeScript) that exports a default function returning a MetadataRoute.Robots object
Next.js generates robots.txt automatically from this file at build time
MetadataRoute.Robots interface: { rules: { userAgent, disallow, allow }[], sitemap: string }
Use NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL env var for the sitemap declaration
Reference: https://nextjs.org/docs/app/api-reference/file-conventions/metadata/robots

stories.title: Menu active category filter state persisted in URL searchParams
stories.description: The currently active menu category filter (display category pill) is held in React state only. Refreshing the page, sharing a link to a filtered view, or navigating back from an item page resets the filter to 'All'. Encoding the active filter as a URL searchParam (?category=vegetarian) makes filtered views shareable and restores the selection on navigation.
acceptanceCriteria: Clicking a category filter pill updates the URL to /[locale]/menu?category=[slug] without a full page reload
Refreshing /[locale]/menu?category=vegetarian renders the menu with the Vegetarian filter pre-selected
Sharing the URL with a category parameter shows the same filtered view to the recipient
When navigating back from a menu item modal, the category filter is restored from the URL
The 'All' filter state is represented as /[locale]/menu (no query param) — not ?category=all
technicalNotes: Use Next.js `useRouter` + `useSearchParams` + `router.push` to update searchParams without full reload
Read initial filter from `useSearchParams().get('category')` on component mount
Use `router.replace` (not push) for filter changes to avoid polluting browser history with each pill click
This is a client component change — MenuFilter is already a client component
Pairs naturally with the menu item detail modal (intercepting routes) for clean URL state management

stories.title: Alt text management for admin-uploaded menu item images
stories.description: Menu item images currently have no alt text beyond the item name used as a fallback. Descriptive alt text is required by WCAG 2.2 SC 1.1.1 (Non-text Content, Level A) and improves image SEO (Google Image Search, Google Lens food discovery). The admin should be able to set a custom alt text per image, with the item name as the default.
acceptanceCriteria: The admin menu editor includes an optional 'Image description (alt text)' text field per menu item
If the field is blank, the alt text defaults to the English item name
The alt text is stored in the menu_items table in a new nullable column `image_alt` (TEXT)
MenuCard renders <Image alt={item.imageAlt ?? item.nameEn} />
Google Search Console > Enhancement > Images shows no 'Missing alt text' issues after rollout
technicalNotes: Add `image_alt TEXT` column to the menu_items table via a DB migration script in scripts/
Update the PATCH /api/admin/menu/[id] handler to accept and persist imageAlt
Update MenuItem TypeScript type in src/types/menu.ts: `imageAlt?: string`
In MenuCard: alt={item.imageAlt || item.nameEn} — never leave alt empty for informative images
For decorative background images (hero), use alt="" to signal decorative intent to screen readers

stories.title: Admin order filter and search by status, date range, and contact number
stories.description: The admin Orders tab shows all orders in a flat list. As order volume grows, finding a specific order (by customer phone, date, or status) requires scrolling through the full list. Server-side filtering and search reduces response payload and helps staff quickly action relevant orders during busy service periods.
acceptanceCriteria: The Orders tab UI has a status filter dropdown (All / Pending / Approved / Payment Uploaded / Preparing / Ready / Rejected)
A date range picker filters orders by created_at date (default: today)
A search input filters by contact_number (partial match, e.g. typing '016' shows all 016-prefix orders)
Filter parameters are sent as query params to GET /api/admin/orders?status=&from=&to=&contact=
The filtered result count is shown ('Showing 3 of 47 orders')
Filter state persists within the admin session (survives tab switching)
technicalNotes: Add query param parsing in GET /api/admin/orders: extract status, from, to, contact from searchParams
SQL: add WHERE clauses conditionally — `WHERE ($1::text IS NULL OR status = $1) AND ...`
Use parameterised queries (not string interpolation) to prevent SQL injection
For the date range, parse to UTC with new Date(from).toISOString() before passing to Neon
Store filter state in a useReducer or Zustand slice in the AdminOrdersPanel component

stories.title: Estimated preparation time shown on customer order status page
stories.description: The customer order status page (/order/[id]) shows the current order status but no indication of when the food will be ready. The admin can already set an estimated_ready timestamp when approving an order. Surfacing this on the customer-facing status page reduces 'where is my order?' friction and sets expectations before arrival.
acceptanceCriteria: When an order has an estimated_ready timestamp and status is 'approved' or 'preparing', the customer status page shows 'Estimated ready: 2:45 PM' (local time, Asia/Kuala_Lumpur timezone)
If estimated_ready has passed but status is still 'preparing', the message changes to 'Should be ready soon'
When status is 'ready', the estimated time is replaced with 'Your order is ready for pickup!'
The estimated time auto-updates without page refresh (the page already polls /api/orders/[id])
The estimated_ready field is already in the orders schema — no DB migration required
technicalNotes: estimated_ready is already in the orders table schema (TIMESTAMPTZ) — just add it to the GET /api/orders/[id] response
Format with Intl.DateTimeFormat('ms-MY', { hour: '2-digit', minute: '2-digit', timeZone: 'Asia/Kuala_Lumpur' })
Add i18n keys: 'order.estimatedReady', 'order.shouldBeReadySoon', 'order.orderReady' to all three message files
The polling interval is already in place — no new infrastructure needed
Edge case: if estimated_ready is null (admin approved without setting it), show 'Preparing your order' without a time

stories.title: Menu item quick-view nutritional and preparation info tooltip
stories.description: Customers with dietary needs (diabetics, those counting calories, allergy sufferers) frequently ask staff about ingredients and preparation. An optional 'Info' field per menu item (stored as free text) surfaced as a tooltip or expandable section on the menu card gives customers this context without requiring a full item detail page.
acceptanceCriteria: Admin menu editor includes an optional 'Preparation notes / Info' text field (max 300 chars) per item
On the menu page, items with a non-empty info field show a small Info icon on the card
Tapping the icon on mobile (or hovering on desktop) shows the info text in a tooltip or slide-up panel
Items without info text show no icon — no visual clutter for the majority of items
The field is stored in a new nullable column `info_text` (TEXT) in menu_items table
technicalNotes: Add `info_text TEXT` column to menu_items via migration script
Use Radix UI Tooltip (already available via shadcn/ui) for desktop; use a bottom sheet or popover for mobile
WCAG: the Tooltip must be keyboard-accessible (focusable trigger, Escape to dismiss)
On mobile, tooltip hover-only behaviour violates WCAG — use a tappable popover instead
Add i18n key 'menu.prepInfo' to all three message files for the icon's aria-label

stories.title: Admin bulk menu item price update via inline editable table
stories.description: When the cafe adjusts prices (e.g. seasonal cost increases, GST/SST recalculations), updating each item individually through the existing single-item editor is time-consuming for a 50+ item menu. An inline-editable price column in the admin menu table allows rapid bulk price review and update in a spreadsheet-like experience.
acceptanceCriteria: The Admin > Menu tab renders a table view mode (in addition to the existing card grid) with columns: Item Name, Category, Price (editable), Availability
Clicking any Price cell makes it inline-editable (input type='number', 2 decimal places, min 0)
A 'Save All Changes' button appears when any price has been modified; it batches all changed prices into a single PATCH /api/admin/menu/bulk request
Unchanged items are excluded from the batch payload
On save success, revalidateTag('menu') is called and a toast confirms the number of items updated
technicalNotes: Track dirty state in a useReducer: { [itemId]: newPrice } — only items with a changed price are in the map
Add PATCH /api/admin/menu/bulk route accepting { updates: [{ id, price }] } array
Use a single Neon transaction for the bulk update to ensure atomicity
Trigger revalidateTag('menu') after the bulk update (pairs with the on-demand ISR story)
Table view vs card view toggle can use a ViewToggle component (Grid / List icons) — shadcn/ui ToggleGroup
dependencies: On-demand menu cache invalidation via revalidateTag after admin edits
